statements.text: The review covers the draft spec before any helpdesk configuration change.
Off-hours billing ticket volume per night is unknown, so queue load cannot be sized.
statements.resolution: Count billing tickets created outside business hours over the last 4 weeks from the helpdesk export.

next_action.action: Support lead answers the d-fallback decision; then the configuration card goes to the engineering path with the test plan.

count_basis.text: Three configuration objects in the existing helpdesk; no code.

evidence.text: Use the existing Europe/Berlin business-hours calendar; do not add a second calendar.

scope_challenge.minimum_change: One queue, one group and one business-hours rule; nothing else is needed for the first release.

architecture.notes: Routing depends on a two-person rota; the spec has no path for a day nobody covers, and rules may not re-run when a tag is added later.

code-quality.notes: Configuration only; the three objects are named and scoped in the spec.

tests.notes: Boundary tests exist for 17:00; daylight-saving changes and the unstaffed day are untested.

performance.notes: One extra rule per ticket; night volume is unknown (s-u-volume), so no load claim is made.

findings.title: No route for a night nobody on the rota covers
findings.problem: With two rota agents, a sick day leaves the off-hours queue unwatched; billing tickets would wait there silently, which is the delay the change is meant to remove.
findings.recommendation: Decide what happens when no rota agent is on shift: fall back to the queue Billing, alert the support lead, or accept the risk for the pilot.

evidence.text: The off-hours rota starts with 2 agents

findings.title: Tag added after creation is not specified
findings.problem: The criteria say 'when the routing rules run' but not whether they run again when the billing tag is added to an existing ticket at night.
findings.recommendation: State in the spec whether re-tagging re-runs routing and add an edge-case test for a ticket tagged billing at 18:00.

findings.title: Daylight-saving change is not in the test plan
findings.problem: The unit test checks 16:59, 17:00 and 08:00 on an ordinary day only; a calendar that switches offset could move the boundary by an hour.
findings.recommendation: Add the boundary test on the last Sunday of March and October.

findings.title: Holiday volume could overload two agents
findings.problem: If public holidays count as off-hours, a holiday could route a full day of billing tickets to two agents.

failure_modes.failure: No rota agent is on shift, so tickets wait in an unwatched queue until the next weekday.
The boundary shifts by one hour around a daylight-saving change.
failure_modes.error_handling: The helpdesk business-hours calendar applies Europe/Berlin daylight saving.

critical_paths.flow: Billing ticket on Friday 18:30 reaches the Off-hours billing queue and a rota agent sees it.
Night with no rota agent on shift: billing ticket at 19:00 follows the d-fallback answer.
Boundary at 17:00 on the last Sunday of March and of October.

edge_cases: Billing tag added at 18:00 to a ticket created at 16:00
Public holiday on a weekday (open spec question)

regression.behavior: Daytime billing tickets still go to the queue Billing.

not_in_scope.reason: The rota calendar stays in the existing scheduling tool.

decisions.question: What happens to an off-hours billing ticket when no rota agent is on shift?

options.label: Route it to the queue Billing as today
Keep it in the off-hours queue and alert the support lead
Accept the risk for the 28-day pilot

decisions.why: It keeps today's behaviour as the floor, so the pilot can only improve on it.

handoff.notes: Configuration card after d-fallback is answered; QA uses test-plan.md.
